categories.title: What you are proving
categories.intro: A security theorem quantifies over every reachable execution trace. Everything below exists to let you say something about such a trace without enumerating it.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.client_secrecy
items.label: client_secrecy
items.must: Assume: a reachable trace, the attacker knows k, and ClientFinishEvent client server xPk yPk k is logged at time.
items.get: The server's signing key was compromised before time, or the client's state for xPk, or the server's state for yPk was compromised.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.client_auth
items.label: client_auth
items.must: Assume: a reachable trace and ClientFinishEvent logged at time.
items.get: The server really ran its finish step with the same shares and key, or its signing key was compromised before time.

categories.title: Reachable traces and the steps that build them
categories.intro: A trace is reachable when it is built from the empty trace by these steps. Each step must come with a Hoare triple; that is what ReachableImpliesInvariant collects, and it is why every reachable trace satisfies the invariant.

items.name: DY.Trace.Reachable
items.label: Trace.Reachable
items.note: Base: the empty trace. Step: run one configured step whose PreCond holds on a reachable trace.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.reachability
items.label: SignedDH reachability
items.note: Generated by #combine: Network (attacker sends), LongTermKeys, the three protocol steps and the three compromise steps. This is the config the theorems quantify over.

items.name: DY.ReachabilityConfig
items.label: ReachabilityConfig
items.note: An Input type, a PreCond on the execution trace, and the Traceful step to run.

items.name: DY.ReachableImpliesInvariant
items.label: ReachableImpliesInvariant
items.must: For every input: a Hoare triple for the step, with pre = PreCond input and post = True.
items.get: The instance that makes Reachable ⇒ Invariant go through for this config.

items.name: DY.Trace.Reachable_implies_Invariant
items.label: Reachable_implies_Invariant
items.get: A proof trace trProof with trProof.Invariant and trProof.erase = trExec.

items.name: DY.Trace.apply_Reachable_implies_Invariant
items.label: apply_Reachable_implies_Invariant
items.get: ∀ trExec, trExec.Reachable config → p trExec. The first tactic of every security theorem.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.Client.initiate
items.label: Client.initiate
items.note: Generate xSk with label clientLabel me xPk, store ClientInitiateState, log ClientInitiateEvent, send xPk.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.Client.initiate.spec
items.label: Client.initiate.spec
items.must: Discharge every append inside the step: the state invariant and the event invariant from what was generated.
items.get: The step is admissible: an instance of ReachableImpliesInvariant for it.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.Server.receive
items.label: Server.receive
items.note: Receive xPk, generate ySk, sign (xPk, yPk) with the long-term key, store ServerFinishState, log ServerFinishEvent, send.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.Server.receive.spec
items.label: Server.receive.spec
items.must: In particular: SignedDHSignPred for the signed message, which needs ServerFinishEvent to be logged before signing.
items.get: The step is admissible.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.Client.finish
items.label: Client.finish
items.note: Receive the server message, verify the signature, derive k, store ClientFinishState, log ClientFinishEvent.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.Client.finish.spec
items.label: Client.finish.spec
items.must: The label of k flows to clientLabel; the event invariant of ClientFinishEvent, by case split on what verify returned.
items.get: The step is admissible. This is where the disjunction in SignedDHEventInv comes from.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.ClientInitiateState.compromise.spec
items.label: ClientInitiateState.compromise.spec
items.get: The attacker may compromise this state at any time; afterwards clientLabel is corrupt.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.ClientFinishState.compromise.spec
items.label: ClientFinishState.compromise.spec
items.get: Same for the finished client state.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.ServerFinishState.compromise.spec
items.label: ServerFinishState.compromise.spec
items.get: Same for the server state; afterwards serverLabel is corrupt.

items.name: DY.Network.instReachableImpliesInvariantReachability
items.label: attacker send step
items.must: PreCond: the attacker knows the message.
items.get: The entry invariant Publishable follows from AttackerKnows_implies_Publishable, so attacker sends preserve the invariant.

items.name: DY.LongTermKeys.generateKeyPair.spec
items.label: generateKeyPair.spec
items.note: Long-term key generation for a named PKI; the secret key gets LongTermKeys.label name p pk.

items.name: DY.LongTermKeys.compromisePrivateKey.spec
items.label: compromisePrivateKey.spec
items.note: Compromising a long-term key is a step the attacker may take; afterwards LongTermKeyCompromised holds.

categories.title: Actions inside a step and their Hoare triples
categories.intro: The step tactic walks a do-block and, at each action, demands the action's precondition and hands you its postcondition. A precondition that mentions the trace is an entry invariant: the price of appending.

items.name: DY.hoareTriple
items.label: hoareTriple
items.note: pre on the proof trace before, Trace.Invariant assumed before and guaranteed after, post on the result and the trace after.

items.name: DY.appendEntry.spec
items.label: appendEntry.spec
items.must: The ghost proof entry erases to the exec entry, and its entry invariant holds on the trace before.
items.get: The entry sits at the returned timestamp. Every action below is built on this.

items.name: DY.Random.genRand.spec
items.label: genRand
items.must: Nothing. You choose the label and the usage as ghost arguments.
items.get: res.Invariant, res.label = label res, res.HasUsage usage.

items.name: DY.Network.sendMessage.spec
items.label: sendMessage
items.get: Nothing; the message is now on the wire and in the attacker's base knowledge.

items.name: DY.Network.receiveMessage.spec
items.label: receiveMessage
items.get: msg.Publishable tr, for whatever was received.

items.name: DY.PersistentLocalState.storeLocalState.spec
items.label: storeLocalState
items.get: A handle.

items.name: DY.PersistentLocalState.getLocalState.spec
items.label: getLocalState
items.get: LocalStateInv.invariant participant st tr for the loaded state.

items.name: DY.PersistentLocalState.compromise.spec
items.label: compromise (local state)
items.get: Nothing directly; the trace now records LocalStateCompromised and the state bytes are sent to the attacker.

items.name: DY.ProtocolEvent.logEvent.spec
items.label: logEvent
items.get: tr.erase.EventLogged ev.

items.name: DY.LongTermKeys.getPublicKey.spec
items.label: getPublicKey
items.get: ProofConfig.IsLongTermPublicKey name p res tr: publishable, labelled, with the PKI's usage.

items.name: DY.LongTermKeys.getPrivateKey.spec
items.label: getPrivateKey
items.get: IsLongTermSecretKey name p res tr: invariant, label lab p pk, usage.

items.label: hash (pure)
items.get: res.Invariant ∧ res.label = b.label.

items.label: dhPk (pure)
items.get: res.Invariant ∧ res.label = Label.pub.

items.label: dh (pure)
items.get: res.label = (sk.label).join (pk.dhSkLabel): the shared secret is as secret as the weaker of the two private shares.

items.label: vk (pure)
items.get: res.Invariant ∧ res.label = Label.pub.

items.label: sign (pure)
items.must: sk has the usage; sk.label flows to the nonce's label; and either SignPred holds for the message or sk's label is already public.
items.get: res.Invariant ∧ res.label = msg.label.

items.label: verify (pure)
items.get: If verification succeeds: SignPred holds for the message, or the signing key's label flows to public.

categories.title: What a trace entry tells you later
categories.intro: The global invariant is the conjunction, over every entry, of that entry's condition on the prefix before it. These are the lemmas that read it back out.

items.name: DY.Trace.Invariant
items.label: Trace.Invariant
items.note: nil ⇒ True; snoc trBefore entry ⇒ trBefore.Invariant ∧ entry.Invariant trBefore.

items.name: DY.SubTraceInvariant
items.label: SubTraceInvariant
items.note: One entry invariant per entry type. The protocol's combined instance is below.

items.name: DY.Trace.invariant_at
items.label: invariant_at
items.get: (tr.at i).Invariant (tr.prefix i).

items.name: DY.Random.instSubTraceInvariantExecEntryTProofEntryT
items.label: random entry
items.note: True. The label and usage live in the ghost proof entry, so they are facts you declared, not facts you proved.

items.name: DY.Random.ProofEntryT
items.label: Random.ProofEntryT
items.note: length, label, usage. erase keeps only the length.

items.name: DY.Network.instSubTraceInvariantExecEntryTProofEntryTOfBytesInvariants
items.label: message entry
items.get: entry.msg.Publishable tr.

items.name: DY.PersistentGlobalState.State.instSubTraceInvariantExecEntryTProofEntryTOfGlobalStateInv
items.label: stored state entry
items.get: The state's GlobalStateInv, which for local states is LocalStateInv.invariant.

items.name: DY.ProtocolEvent.instSubTraceInvariantExecEntryTProofEntryTOfEventInv
items.label: event entry
items.get: EventInv.invariant tr entry.ev.

items.name: DY.Trace.EventLoggedAt_imp_EventInv
items.label: EventLoggedAt_imp_EventInv
items.get: EventInv.invariant (tr.prefix i) ev.

items.name: DY.Trace.EventLogged_imp_EventInv
items.label: EventLogged_imp_EventInv
items.get: ∃ i, EventInv.invariant (tr.prefix i) ev.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.instSubTraceInvariantExecEntryTProofEntryT
items.label: SignedDH combined entry invariant
items.note: Generated by #combine from the entry invariants of every entry type this protocol uses.

categories.title: SignedDH's own invariants: the author's choices
categories.intro: These are the only places where the protocol author decides what the trace must guarantee. Too weak and the theorems do not follow; too strong and a step cannot establish them.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.SignedDHEventInv
items.label: SignedDHEventInv
items.get: ClientInitiate: xPk's secret label is clientLabel. ServerFinish: kS's label is serverLabel ⊔ xPk's secret label. ClientFinish: the server finished with the same k and k's label is clientLabel ⊔ serverLabel, OR a server signing key is corrupt.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.ClientInitiateStateInv
items.label: ClientInitiateStateInv
items.get: xPk = dhPk xSk, xPk publishable, xSk invariant with label clientLabel me xPk.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.ClientFinishStateInv
items.label: ClientFinishStateInv
items.get: kC invariant and its label flows to clientLabel me xPk.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.ServerFinishStateInv
items.label: ServerFinishStateInv
items.get: kS invariant and its label flows to serverLabel me yPk.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.SignedDHSignPred
items.label: SignedDHSignPred
items.must: To sign (xPk, yPk) with the server's long-term key: yPk is dhPk ySk with label serverLabel, and ServerFinishEvent is already logged.
items.get: When a signature verifies under an honest key, exactly this.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.instProofConfigMkLongTermUsageLabel
items.label: "SignedDH PKI" ProofConfig
items.get: IsLongTermPublicKey: the verification key is publishable, labelled LongTermKeys.label, and has the server's signing usage.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.clientLabel
items.label: clientLabel
items.note: Corrupt iff ClientEphemeralStateCompromised client xPk.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.serverLabel
items.label: serverLabel
items.note: Corrupt iff ServerEphemeralStateCompromised server yPk.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.ClientEphemeralStateCompromised
items.label: ClientEphemeralStateCompromised
items.note: Either client state holding xPk was compromised.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.ServerEphemeralStateCompromised
items.label: ServerEphemeralStateCompromised
items.note: The server state holding yPk was compromised.

items.name: DY.Example.SignedDH.mkLongTermUsage
items.label: mkLongTermUsage
items.note: The usage tag that ties a signing key to a server name; SignPred matches on it.

categories.title: Bytes: labels, usages and structural invariants
categories.intro: A byte string's label and invariant are computed from how it was built, one rule per primitive. The invariant means the bytes were made legitimately, so the label can be trusted.

items.name: DY.Bytes.Invariant
items.label: Bytes.Invariant
items.note: Recursion over the structure of the bytes using each primitive's invariant rule.

items.name: DY.Bytes.label
items.label: Bytes.label
items.note: Recursion over the structure using each primitive's label rule.

items.name: DY.Bytes.HasUsage
items.label: Bytes.HasUsage
items.note: Usages separate keys by purpose, e.g. a signing key for one PKI.

items.name: DY.Bytes.Publishable
items.label: Publishable
items.get: b.Invariant ∧ (b.label).canFlow Label.pub. Everything the attacker knows is publishable.

items.name: DY.Bytes.KnowableBy
items.label: KnowableBy
items.get: b.Invariant ∧ (b.label).canFlow l: the bytes may flow to anything with label l.

items.name: DY.Bytes.label_later
items.label: label_later
items.get: Labels of well-formed bytes do not change as the trace grows.

items.name: DY.Bytes.Publishable_later_fast
items.label: Publishable_later
items.get: Publishable is preserved by trace extension.

items.name: DY.Random.Random.invariants
items.label: random bytes rule
items.get: Invariant: a random entry exists at the timestamp with this label and usage. Label: that entry's label.

items.name: DY.Literal.Literal.invariants
items.label: literal rule
items.get: Public constants: label pub.

items.name: DY.Concat.Concat.invariants
items.label: concat rule
items.get: Label of a concatenation is the meet of its parts' labels.

items.name: DY.Hash.Hash.invariants
items.label: hash rule
items.get: Label of a hash is the label of its input.

items.name: DY.DiffieHellman.DhPk.invariants
items.label: dhPk rule
items.get: A public share is public; dhSkLabel remembers the private share's label.

items.name: DY.DiffieHellman.Dh.invariants
items.label: dh rule
items.get: A shared secret's label is the join of the two private shares' labels.

items.label: signature rule
items.get: Invariant: SignPred held for the message under the key's usage, or the key's label flows to public. Label: the message's label.

items.name: DY.Signature.SignPred
items.label: SignPred
items.note: The per-protocol promise a signer makes. SignedDHSignPred instantiates it.

items.name: DY.Bytes.dhSkLabel
items.label: dhSkLabel
items.note: The label of the private share behind a public DH share.

items.name: DY.Bytes.signkeyLabel
items.label: signkeyLabel
items.note: The label of the signing key behind a verification key.

categories.title: Labels, flows and corruption
categories.intro: A label is a predicate on execution traces saying when it is corrupt. canFlow orders labels by corruption, and every secrecy claim is a statement about a label being corrupt.

items.name: DY.Label
items.label: Label
items.note: Just isCorrupt : ExecTrace → Prop.

items.name: DY.Label.canFlow
items.label: canFlow
items.get: l1.canFlow l2 tr: for every later trace, l2 corrupt ⇒ l1 corrupt.

items.name: DY.canFlowTrans
items.label: canFlowTrans
items.get: canFlow is transitive.

items.name: DY.Label.pub
items.label: Label.pub
items.note: Always corrupt. canFlow pub therefore means: corrupt now.

items.name: DY.Label.secret
items.label: Label.secret
items.note: Never corrupt.

items.name: DY.Label.join
items.label: Label.join
items.note: Corrupt iff either side is corrupt. The label of a value that two parties both know.

items.name: DY.Label.joinIsCorrupt
items.label: joinIsCorrupt
items.get: (l1.join l2).isCorrupt tr ↔ l1.isCorrupt tr ∨ l2.isCorrupt tr.

items.name: DY.Label.joinCanFlowLeft
items.label: joinCanFlowLeft
items.get: l1.canFlow (l1.join l2).

items.name: DY.LongTermKeys.label
items.label: LongTermKeys.label
items.note: Corrupt iff LongTermKeyCompromised for that PKI, participant and key.

items.name: DY.LongTermKeys.LongTermKeyCompromised
items.label: LongTermKeyCompromised
items.note: Some secret key whose public key is pk was in a compromised local state.

items.name: DY.PersistentLocalState.LocalStateCompromised
items.label: LocalStateCompromised
items.note: A compromise entry for exactly this participant and state is in the trace.

items.name: DY.PersistentLocalState.CompromisableLocalStateInv
items.label: CompromisableLocalStateInv
items.must: invariant_implies_KnowableBy: every byte string in the state is knowable by the state's label.
items.get: So compromising the state may hand its contents to the attacker without breaking the invariant.

categories.title: Attacker knowledge
categories.intro: The attacker's knowledge is a least fixpoint: base knowledge from the trace, closed under every primitive. One theorem per primitive shows publishability is preserved, so the whole fixpoint is publishable.

items.name: DY.Bytes.AttackerKnows
items.label: AttackerKnows
items.note: The least set containing the base knowledge and closed under the attacker rules of every primitive.

items.name: DY.Bytes.AttackerKnows.is_least_fixpoint
items.label: is_least_fixpoint
items.must: A predicate that contains the base knowledge and is closed under each rule.
items.get: Every attacker-known byte string satisfies it.

items.name: DY.Bytes.AttackerKnows_implies_Publishable
items.label: AttackerKnows_implies_Publishable
items.get: b.Publishable tr, hence (b.label tr).isCorrupt tr.erase. grind fires this automatically.

items.name: DY.Trace.BaseAttackerKnows
items.label: BaseAttackerKnows
items.note: Messages on the wire and compromised state contents.

items.name: DY.Trace.BaseAttackerKnows_implies_Publishable
items.label: BaseAttackerKnows_implies_Publishable
items.get: The base case of the fixpoint argument, from the message entry invariant and CompromisableLocalStateInv.

items.name: DY.AttackerKnowledgeTheorem
items.label: AttackerKnowledgeTheorem
items.note: The per-primitive closure proofs, combined for the protocol's set of primitives.
